title: Whittled ash letter opener
subtitle: A thin, stiff blade for opening envelopes
excerpt: A letter opener in seasoned ash: 22 cm overall, a 10 cm blade flat on one face and angled on the other, and a smooth oval handle. Knife-only work, danish-oil finish. The thin blade requires careful grain management at the tip.
sourceNotes: Sloyd school knife-exercise patterns from Otto Salomon, The Theory of Educational Sloyd (1892).

glossaryTerms.definition: Air-dried or kiln-dried wood at a stable moisture content for indoor use (8 to 12 per cent). Does not shrink after working.
A section of wood where the grain direction runs across the narrow dimension of the piece, leaving only a short fibre length supporting the section. Short grain is fragile.

content.text: A letter opener is a blunt-bladed knife shape: long, thin, stiff, with a rounded tip that can run under a gummed flap without puncturing the envelope. At 22 cm overall, it suits a desktop or a desk drawer. This project uses
seasoned wood
ash for its stiffness in thin section: a 5 mm ash blade will not flex during use, whereas an equivalent pine blade would.
Before you start cutting.
Grip: four-finger grip on the work; thumb-push grip on the knife. Never make a cut whose blade-path can reach a body part.
Cut direction: push cuts (blade away from body) and thumb-pivot cuts are the default. Pull cuts only with the work braced against the chest and the blade-arc unable to reach anything vital.
Sharpening: a dull tool is more dangerous than a sharp one. The dull tool slips. Strop every fifteen minutes of carving, hone weekly, oilstone monthly.
First aid: keep a styptic pencil, gauze, and a clean dressing within reach. Apply firm pressure, elevate, and dress. A cut that shows fat or won't close with pressure goes to A&E, not a plaster.
Workspace: stable seat, good light, no children or pets within arm-and-blade reach.
Wood
Ash in the
seasoned

state from a PAR board or from a straight section of branch. Ash is the preferred species because the grain runs very straight in good boards and the open grain gives a clean knife finish. A board 19 mm thick provides enough material; a 24 cm length is the starting blank. Maple is the best alternative: harder, finer, and also very strong in thin section.
Tools
Sloyd knife: all shaping.
Detail knife (optional): for finishing the blade taper and tip.
Leather strop: strop every fifteen minutes.
Danish oil: penetrating finish for a desk item.
Method
Step 1: Mark the plan

Draw the letter opener on the wide face of the blank. The blade is 10 cm long and 2.5 cm wide at the shoulder, tapering evenly to 8 mm at the tip. The handle is 12 cm long, 2.5 cm wide at the shoulder, 2 cm at the end. The whole piece is flat in plan at this stage.
Step 2: Cut the plan outline
Push cuts with the
sloyd knife
to remove waste outside the lines. Ash is harder than pine; keep the edge well stropped.
Step 3: Taper the blade from one face

The blade is flat on one face (the underside) and angled on the other. Turn the blank flat-face down. Use push cuts to reduce the upper face of the blade from 19 mm at the shoulder to 5 mm at the tip. The angle of cut is gentle, about 7 degrees. Work from shoulder to tip, keeping the angle consistent, and check with a ruler every few strokes.
Step 4: The blade tip
The tip of a letter opener is rounded, not pointed. The tip section is
short-grain

: only a few mm of wood support the last centimetre. Do not make long cuts into the tip from one direction. Instead, make very short push cuts from each side of the tip alternately, meeting in the centre. If the tip breaks off, the blade is salvageable: round the break to a new tip, which will be 1 to 2 cm shorter but still functional.
Step 5: Round the handle

Use the four-sided to eight-sided to oval sequence to round the handle. The handle on a letter opener is slightly slimmer than on a spoon: 2 cm finished diameter is comfortable for most hands and does not feel bulky in a desk drawer.
Finishing

Apply danish oil with a cloth. Three coats, one per day. Cure for five to seven days. The blade can be given a light buff with 0000 wire wool after the first coat to knock back any grain rise, then wiped clean before the second coat.
Variations
Decorate the handle with chip-carved triangles in a band around the shoulder.
Make matching letter openers in ash and maple and give them as a paired desk set.

attrs.cause: The cut ran past the short grain at the tip.
attrs.fix: Round the break to a clean curve and continue. The opener is still usable at a slightly shorter length.

attrs.symptom: The blade has a twist along its length
attrs.cause: The taper cut on one face was not kept parallel to the flat underside.
attrs.fix: Check the blade with a straight edge every five strokes. Correct any twist by removing more material from the high edge only.
